findings.text: git commit --only snapshots the entire current roster file, so a prior default-off registration is absorbed into the next public add commit; the probe produced subject chore(roster): register public-b with both internal-a and public-b, recreating a commit whose message describes one change and whose content carries two.
the commit-boundary fixture always starts from a clean repository, so it cannot catch an earlier legitimate non-committing roster write being swept into the public member-add commit.

justifications.durability: tests/test_roster_write_commits.py:33 guards a clean public add and line 79 guards the default-off caller, but neither test composes those two states to detect same-file absorption.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_roster_write_commits.py:33 plus defect-reproduction.log and the paired all_debug receipts prove the clean-start case and preserve a 34-to-34 failure-id delta, but do not exercise pre-existing roster dirt.
justifications.fit: reckon/ledger.py:705 uses a mechanism-named private helper and an explicit default-off option with no forbidden plan labels, while keeping the CLI opt-in at reckon/cli.py:2949.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:750 commits the whole current roster path, and an independent probe showed a prior internal-a write folded into the commit whose subject named only public-b.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat for 588c56c4, 0b73f64e, and 35c00234 names only the five paths in the extended manifest fence, including the coordinator-granted reckon/cli.py path.
